about: Step-named mutation registry (LIMBO-29). Each mutation is applied to a disposable copy of the package; 'kills' is the check that must stop passing. 'repin': true re-pins the mutated file's sha256 everywhere in src/ and RELEASE-MANIFEST.json (a forgery that keeps LIMBO-26 green); 'regen' (a name or a list) re-generates artifacts of record in the copy and re-pins them: 'simulate' the census (a cheaper or different experiment posing as the pinned one), 'rtp-table' the RTP table, 'record' the verification record; 'parts' edits several files; 'expectExit' (a code or a list) is the exit the run must end in for the mutation to count as killed (an RTP miss with the table and record regenerated ends in 5, the same change unregenerated in 1; a missing step in 3). 'op': 'rm' deletes 'file' from the copy; 'truncate' keeps the first floor(n·value) records of the array at 'path' ('coherent': every other count in the file that equalled n is set to the new length); 'null' sets 'keys' to null in every record of the array at 'path'. M01n, M05s and M20d (30 Oct 2026): every reveal null, the dataset cut to 80 %, the census deleted; a verifier that throws on one of them prints no row for the check it names, which this battery scores as a survivor, so each must leave its check FAIL with every row printed. 'repinPackage': true (with 'repin') also replaces the mutated file's sha256 in the copy's MANIFEST.md and README.md ('repin' already covers src/ and RELEASE-MANIFEST.json), so that no pin and no quoted hash can catch the change. M24a and M24b (17 Nov 2026) cover LIMBO-24: M24a changes the site-verifier module and re-pins it everywhere, so only the side-by-side run with src/rng.ts can catch it; M24b breaks the module's pin in src/artifact-pins.ts and leaves the module alone.
